expectations.text: It includes a humanizing pass over headlines, primary text, and descriptions before final delivery, rather than shipping raw first-draft output.
expectations.evidence: No humanizing/de-slop step is mentioned anywhere: the process notes cover assumptions, angle selection, character limits, compliance, and a six-check distinctness gate (generic test, one angle per variant, proof traceability, surface fit, message match, label completeness) — none of which is a voice/naturalness pass, and no 'read aloud', 'strip AI tells', or rewrite step is claimed. The delivered copy still carries first-draft AI tells: decorative emoji appended to every headline and several body lines (🪑 ⚡ 🧍 💪), an em-dash triad ('apps, sticky notes, willpower'), and near-identical parallel c

expectations.text: In drafted variants, the headline complements the primary text rather than repeating it.
expectations.evidence: Most pairs divide labor cleanly: 'back pain isn't always a mattress problem' + body pivoting to the chair/eight hours; 'the 9-to-5 crowd who forgot to stand up straight' + 'You didn't choose to sit eight hours a day — your job did'; 'Peakform fixes posture while you forget it exists' + body explaining why reminder-based fixes fail. Two IG rows show mild echo rather than true complement: 'posture, auto-corrected' against a body ending 'so good posture becomes automatic', and 'stand taller, by default' against a body about being nudged 'back to straighter... posture'. No explicit complementarity

expectations.text: It includes a humanizing pass over headlines, primary text, and descriptions before final delivery, rather than shipping raw first-draft output.
expectations.evidence: The transcript is a single delivery of finished copy with no sign of any revision or de-slop/humanizing stage: no before/after, no mention of rewriting for natural voice, no reference to a humanizer step. The 'Notes' section only justifies brand placement, the education hook, emoji count, and why the 60 Trustpilot reviews were omitted — all first-draft rationale, not evidence of a pass over the assets. Some lines do read conversationally ('You blame your chair, your mattress, your age'), but that is an attribute of the draft, not evidence of a humanizing pass; several assets still carry tellta

expectations.evidence: Mixed. Genuine complementarity in LinkedIn B (headline adds the 'no effort required' promise while intro runs the mattress/age reframe) and Instagram A (headline 'Peakform fixes posture, not just pain' adds a positioning claim the body's 'Back pain? Not your mattress' does not). But LinkedIn A repeats its own payoff — headline 'stops back pain before it starts' vs intro 'before the pain starts'; LinkedIn C echoes the literal phrase 'sit up straight' in both headline and intro; Instagram B's headline 'Peakform.
